prompt: What is the `veth…` interface that appeared on the host when `box-a` started?

choices.text: A copy of the host's network card, made for the container
choices.why: It is virtual, and one end of a pair.

choices.text: The host's end of a pair with `eth0` inside
choices.why: Right, plugged into `docker0`.

choices.text: A firewall rule Docker adds for the bridge
choices.why: It is an interface; rules are elsewhere.

choices.text: The DNS server that answers the containers' names
choices.why: DNS is `127.0.0.11`, inside the container.

prompt: Inside `box-a`, the default route goes via `___`, the address of `docker0`.
On the default bridge, `ping box-a` from `box-b` gave `bad address`, and the address worked. Why?

choices.text: `box-a` does not answer pings
choices.why: It answered the ping by address.

choices.text: Names need a `docker network connect` first, on every container
choices.why: Connecting changes networks; the default bridge still has no names.

choices.text: Nothing there resolves container names
choices.why: Right; a user-defined network does.

choices.text: The names had a typo
choices.why: `box-a` was the exact name.

prompt: On `shelfnet`, what answered the lookup for `shelf-web`?

choices.text: Google's DNS at `8.8.8.8`, through the host
choices.why: That is where other questions are passed on.

choices.text: The host's `/etc/hosts`, copied in at start
choices.why: The host's files were not involved.

choices.text: `shelf-web` announcing itself on the network
choices.why: Containers announce nothing; Docker answers.

choices.text: Docker's embedded DNS at `127.0.0.11`
choices.why: Right: it knows every container on the network by name.

prompt: From the default bridge, `box-a` could not reach `shelf-web` even by its address. What changed that?

choices.text: `docker network connect shelfnet box-a`
choices.why: Right: a second interface, on `shelfnet`.

choices.text: Publishing port 8080 with `-p`
choices.why: Publishing is for the host's side, not between bridges.

choices.text: Restarting `box-a` so it got a new address
choices.why: A new address on the same bridge changes nothing.

choices.text: Turning off the host's firewall
choices.why: Never the fix; the isolation is wanted.

prompt: Why put a database on a `backend` network that the web-facing proxy is not on?
hint: What does a separate bridge do?

choices.text: Separate networks make database queries faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: Only containers on `backend` reach it
choices.why: Right: whatever is compromised on `frontend` cannot even see it.

choices.text: Postgres refuses the default bridge
choices.why: It runs fine there.

choices.text: Compose needs a separate network for every service
choices.why: One per project is the default.

prompt: `shelf` listens on the host's `127.0.0.1:8080`. Why does `localhost:8080` from `box-c` get `Connection refused`?

choices.text: `box-c` has no `wget` installed in its image
choices.why: `wget` ran and reported the refusal.

choices.text: The port was published to the wrong address
choices.why: Ana's own `curl` reached it.

choices.text: There, `localhost` is `box-c`
choices.why: Right: nothing listens on `box-c`'s own 8080.

choices.text: Alpine blocks port 8080 by default
choices.why: Alpine blocks nothing of the kind.

prompt: `host.docker.internal:8080` was refused, though the name resolved to `172.17.0.1`. Why?

choices.text: `host-gateway` works only under Docker Desktop, not Engine
choices.why: It resolved and connected on the next try.

choices.text: Containers may never reach the host
choices.why: The third attempt reached it.

choices.text: Port 8080 is reserved for `docker0`
choices.why: Nothing reserves it; it is about the listening address.

choices.text: Only on `127.0.0.1`, not the bridge's address
choices.why: Right; the service on every address answered.

prompt: Match each network mode to what the container gets.

pairs.right: Its own namespace, reachable by address
Its own namespace, reachable by name
The host's own interfaces and ports

right_distractors: A copy of every other container's network

prompt: With `--network host -e PORT=9090`, on which host port did `ss` show `shelf` listening?
`shelf` and Postgres run on one server; only `shelf` should be reachable, and only through a proxy on the same machine. Which layout?
hint: Names between them, one loopback door outward.

choices.text: One user network for both; publish `shelf` on `127.0.0.1` only
choices.why: Right: `db` by name inside, one loopback door outside.

choices.text: Both on `--network host`
choices.why: Postgres would listen on the machine itself.

choices.text: Both on the default bridge, by address
choices.why: Addresses change on restart, and nothing resolves names.

choices.text: Publish both on every address and rely on `ufw`
choices.why: Lesson 17: Docker's rules come before `ufw`'s.
